text:
Noah Ostlund has been handed a much bigger job in Buffalo this season. The 22-year-old Swede is playing 18:13 a night, up from 13:58, and is on the ice for 64% of the Sabres' power-play time after 15% last season. A Buffalo News headline summed up why: "He's just a tool that you can use, anywhere."

His own game has grown with it. His chances are up to 0.85 expected goals per 60 minutes (the quality of his shots) from 0.45, and he has 12 points in 22 games. It should be more: Buffalo has scored 8.8 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, the kind of gap that usually swings back.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows his style: 67% of his shots came off the rush last season, and 20% of his setups crossed the royal road, the side-to-side pass that moves a goalie, against 7% for a typical forward. Evolving-Hockey had his value coming mostly from defense. One thing to watch: his ice time dipped to about 13 to 15 minutes in his last three games.
headline: Noah Ostlund's bigger role deserves more points
